"CreateDataflowGraph request creates a new graph"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Create-graph response variant and nonempty unique graph IDs are asserted for each raw session.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Original Scala suite is unexecuted.

cases.name_expression: "create dataflow graph falls back to current database in session"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Graph created without defaults captures the active database; subsequent output response still uses it after the session changes databases.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Internal GraphDefinition.defaultDatabase is inferred from resolved output, not directly inspected.

cases.name_expression:
"create dataflow graph set session catalog and database to pipeline " +
      "default catalog and database"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Explicit graph catalog/database update current session catalog/database and resolve an output with the captured values after session database changes.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Uses the configured catalog, not a second catalog. Internal GraphDefinition fields are inferred through responses, not inspected.

cases.name_expression: "Define a flow for a graph that does not exist"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Define-output against a missing graph rejects with DATAFLOW_GRAPH_NOT_FOUND; port additionally checks mapped exception, graphId parameter and SQL state.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Original Scala uses an Exception message substring check and a populated DefineOutput (name mv/type MATERIALIZED_VIEW); port uses minimal command and structured condition. Original Scala transport test is unexecuted.

cases.name_expression: "Define flow 'once' argument not supported"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Explicit once=true and once=false reject with DEFINE_FLOW_ONCE_OPTION_NOT_SUPPORTED. Ports also check AnalysisException, flowName and SQL state, with missing/existing graphs and omitted/named flow names.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Original Scala grid and its message assertion have not executed against Sail; ports assert structured condition through the Python client.

coverage_review.covered_assertions: None mapped in this audit.

cases.name_expression: "dataflow graphs are session-specific"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Separate user/session combinations can register their own datasets. Cross-session registration rejects foreign graphs; cross-session drop leaves the owner intact. Same-user distinct-session control is included.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Original registry counts and graph-definition dataset contents are not inspected. Reusing one session ID across users is not tested; original source also uses distinct session IDs.

cases.name_expression: "dataflow graphs are cleaned up when session is closed"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: None mapped in this audit.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Close session, inspect session manager absence and retained holder graph registry empty.

cases.name_expression: "multiple dataflow graphs can exist in the same session"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Two graphs in one session register and execute independent SQL materialized outputs. The second output is absent after the first run; it remains executable after dropping the first graph. First output data survives.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Original test registers only output definitions and directly inspects each internal graph table collection; this port observes SQL registration and persisted results instead. Original Scala suite is unexecuted.

cases.name_expression: "dropping a dataflow graph removes it from session"

coverage_review.covered_assertions: Dropped graph becomes unavailable for a later start; published table stays readable.
coverage_review.remaining_assertions: Internal graph-registry size transitions one to zero and the unexecuted registered-output fixture are not directly checked.
